desc:
Failed payment recovery and dunning emails, set up by Ecom Swift LLC. We configure smart retries, polite reminders and in-app notices so a declined card becomes a quick fix instead of a lost subscriber.

## What is failed payment recovery?

Failed payment recovery is the process that runs when a recurring charge does not go through. Cards expire, limits are reached, banks block unfamiliar charges and cards get replaced after fraud alerts. The customer usually does not know it happened and never meant to leave. Recovery means retrying the charge at sensible times, telling the customer clearly, and making it easy for them to fix the payment.

Emails sent during this process are often called dunning emails. The word sounds harsh, but good dunning is helpful and calm: a short message, a clear reason and one button to update the card.

## Why involuntary churn deserves attention

Customers who leave on purpose are lost because of the product, the price or a competitor. Customers who leave because of a failed payment are lost because of a card. This second group is often the easiest to win back, since the intent to pay is still there. Without a recovery process, those accounts simply cancel after a few silent retries, and nobody on your team notices.

Recovery works through timing and clarity. A retry a few days later succeeds when a temporary hold has cleared. An email that arrives at the right moment, with a direct link, reaches the customer while they still remember the product. A banner inside the app reaches the people who never read email. Together they raise the chance that the payment is fixed before access ends, although results depend on your customers, your plans and your bank mix.

## What a good recovery flow includes

- A retry schedule configured in your billing provider, spaced over several days.
- A branded failed-payment email with a link that opens the card update form.
- A short sequence of follow-up emails, each with a different tone and deadline.
- A banner or notice inside the app for logged-in customers.
- A grace period during which access continues, so loyal customers are not cut off at once.
- A card-expiry warning sent before the card actually fails.
- A final notice before the subscription is cancelled.
- Account status saved in your database, so support can see who is in recovery.
- Rules by plan or customer size, so large accounts get a personal touch.
- A report showing how much revenue was recovered.

## How we set it up

We first review your provider's built-in retry and email tools, because they often cover the basics well. Then we decide with you what should happen to access: full use during the grace period, limited use after it, then cancellation. The Basic package sets the retry schedule, adds one branded email and tests the flow with a declining test card. The Standard package adds a three-step sequence, an in-app banner, a grace period and expiry warnings. The Premium package adds rules by plan, alerts to your team for high-value failures, a final notice, a recovered revenue report and a handover call.

Throughout, we keep the tone helpful. The emails state the facts, avoid blame and give one clear action. Ecom Swift LLC cannot promise a particular recovery rate, since bank behavior and customer habits vary.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Send the first email promptly, while the customer still remembers the product.
- Put one clear button in every message that opens the card update form.
- Keep access running through a fair grace period.
- Warn customers before a card expires.
- Tell your support team how to see accounts in recovery.

**Avoid:**
- Writing threatening or guilt-heavy emails.
- Sending daily reminders with the same wording.
- Cutting off access on the first failed attempt.
- Asking customers to reply by email with card details.
- Ignoring failed payments on your largest accounts.

## Who this is for

This service suits a subscription business that has noticed customers disappearing without a cancel request. It suits a team with many monthly card payments and no process for declines. It also suits a founder who relies on provider defaults and wants the tone, timing and in-app notices to match the brand.

## What we need and how to start

Tell us which billing provider you use, how long a grace period you prefer and what limited access should look like. Send your logo and any email wording you already like. We need developer or collaborator access to your app and a team role in your provider account, and never your passwords. After you order, we send a short checklist and a test run of the full recovery flow.
